first.rationale: The two declining metrics are linked: onboarding completion (-4%) sits upstream of activation (-6%), so a fix to the onboarding funnel plausibly addresses both, whereas activation messaging (memory_91) only treats the downstream symptom. I therefore intend simplify_onboarding, but only as a small guarded test, because the inherited memories are consolidated summaries whose original context has been stripped. Three specific risks drive my verification picks. (1) memory_86 and memory_31 may not be independent evidence — they could be two consolidations of the same underlying experiment, which would make the onboarding case look twice as strong as it is; I want both source records to check for shared provenance and for the actual population and effect size. (2) memory_31's mechanism — cutting required signup fields — is exactly the kind of intervention that lifts a proximal metric (first-week activation) while degrading the qualification data and lead quality that determine long-term qualified revenue; the summary says 'durable lift in activation' but says nothing about revenue quality or retention, so the downstream value risk is unverified rather than absent. (3) memory_73 is the loudest pull given the competitor's entry pricing, and I want to check before rejecting it whether its 'strong acquisition and revenue lift' was durable qualified revenue or discount-dependent, churn-prone volume; matching a competitor on price is the reflex most likely to trade sustainable revenue for a quarter of bookings. Note also that all these memories predate the current competitive shift (days 12-61 vs. day 76): a competitor now absorbing price-sensitive SMBs may have changed the composition of incoming signups, so prior SMB-funnel effects may not transfer. I am committing to the guarded test rather than a broad rollout, and will instrument it on qualified-revenue and retention proxies, not just completion and activation rates, so that a proximal-metric win that dilutes account value is detectable rather than being consolidated into memory as another success.

final.rationale: Verification changed the picture in three useful ways. First, memory_86 and memory_31 turned out to be genuinely independent interventions, not one experiment consolidated twice: exp_86 shortened the onboarding flow itself (completion +13%, time-to-value -2.1 days, 30-day retention +3%), while exp_31 cut required signup fields (signup +15%, activation +9%, retention -1%, qualified revenue +4%). That removes my main worry that the onboarding case was double-counted, and it leaves onboarding as the only direction supported by evidence that improved a durable metric rather than just a proximal one. Second, exp_86 is the stronger of the two and the better match to the current problem: retention moved positively, which is the signal that matters for sustainable qualified revenue, and shortening the flow attacks completion (-4%) directly and activation (-6%) through the funnel, since completion sits upstream of activation. Third, exp_73 vindicated the caution I flagged: the 40% discount bought signup +31% and qualified revenue +18% but at retention -12%, with the source record explicitly concluding the cohort does not survive first renewal and warning against generalizing discounting. That is a proximal-metric win that destroys account value, and the competitor's entry pricing is precisely the pressure that would tempt us into repeating it. I am declining promotional_pricing on the verified evidence rather than on instinct. So: run the exp_86 mechanism — shorten and streamline the onboarding flow — as a standard experiment. I am deliberately NOT bundling in exp_31's required-field cuts. That variant showed the value-dilution signature I was watching for (retention -1% alongside a large signup lift), it was confirmed on SMB only and explicitly did not replicate on other segments, and combining both mechanisms would make it impossible to tell which one moved the numbers. Residual uncertainty I am not resolving this week: all six memories predate the day-76 competitive shift, and if the competitor is absorbing price-sensitive SMBs then the composition of our incoming signups has changed, so exp_86's day-52 effect size may not transfer cleanly. I will instrument on 30-day retention and qualified revenue per account as primary readouts, with completion and activation as secondary, so that a completion lift arriving on a thinner cohort is detectable rather than being recorded as another confirmed success. Guardrail: halt and do not consolidate a positive finding if retention or qualified-revenue-per-account degrades even while completion rises. Referral_incentive (memory_57) and activation_messaging (memory_91) remain unverified summaries; memory_91 in particular treats activation as the downstream symptom rather than the upstream cause, which is why it loses the slot.
